transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, what brought me in is that... lately, some evenings after work, I just end up eating way more than I ever intended to. Especially if I've been really strict with my diet all day. I'll have dinner, and then... I don't know, I just keep going. I'll have a bowl of cereal, some crackers, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and then sweets, all within just a couple of hours. It just feels like too much.
During these times when you keep eating, do you feel like you are unable to stop or control how much you eat?

Yeah, I do. Once I get started on those nights, it's like... I just keep going back to the kitchen. Even while I'm telling myself to stop, I just don't. I don't really feel back in charge of what I'm doing until I'm uncomfortably full.
After these episodes, do you do anything to try to make up for what you ate, such as making yourself vomit or using laxatives?

No, I don't make myself throw up or use laxatives or anything like that. But... the next day after one of those nights, I definitely try to make up for it. I'll usually skip breakfast and lunch entirely. Or I'll force myself to take an extra-long hike, or push myself a lot harder at softball conditioning, even if I'm really tired and sore. I just feel like I have to burn it all off.
Could you tell me your current height and approximately how much you weigh?
I'm 5 foot 4. As for my weight... I'm not exactly sure right at this moment. I haven't stepped on a scale in a little while, but I usually hover right around 145 pounds.
On average, about how many times a week do these episodes happen?

Well, for the past few months, I'd say it's been happening most weeks. Usually it's about one or two nights a week where I end up eating far more than I planned to. And then, like I mentioned, the next day I try to make up for it by skipping meals or exercising a lot longer.
How much does your body shape or weight influence how you feel about yourself as a person?

Well, it definitely has an impact. Like... if my waistband feels tight before a client luncheon or a leadership meeting, I just start feeling like I look sloppy. I start worrying that people won't take me as seriously, even though I know I've still been doing my job well. It just really messes with my confidence and how I see myself.

latest_inference.note: Confirmed overvaluation of shape/weight influencing self-evaluation, meeting all criteria for Bulimia nervosa (F50.2) and ruling out F50.8.
